To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a gene functional association interactome for anti-angiogenesis drug activity assessment in an in vitro co-culture model, and that the interactome is useful to simulate network perturbation caused by multi-targeted antiangiogenic kinase inhibitors, which correlates well with observed drug activity in a cord bioassay.

1) we established a comprehensive gene association network to model angiogenesis, 2) we applied a network perturbation algorithm to simulate the effect of multi-targeted kinase inhibitors on angiogenesis, and 3) simulated network perturbation correlated well with observed drug activity in a cord bioassay.
a comprehensive gene functional network was constructed and used to simulate the level at which a network was perturbed by three multi-target anti-angiogenic compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing an in vitro angiogenic model and applying network analysis to understand angiogenic regulation and to predict drug activity.
the development of a gene functional association interactome for modeling angiogenesis and the application of the resulting network to anti-angiogenesis drug efficacy evaluation.
the development and application of a gene functional association interactome for antiangiogenic drug assessment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study developed and applied a global functional association model to simulate drug phenotypic activities in vitro.
our work provided a proof-of-principle pilot for applying a network perturbation analysis approach to drug phenotypically related activity assessment.
we developed a gene functional association model to simulate angiogenesis regulation and to assess the anti-angiogenic activity of kinase inhibitors in a co-culture model of angiogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a functional gene association network can serve as a platform to facilitate the understanding of angiogenesis regulation and to aid anti-angiogenesis drug discovery.
the present interactome could be a valuable tool for anti-angiogenesis research and development.
the network perturbation approach is a viable strategy to predict anti-angiogenesis efficacy of multi-targeted kinase inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
network analysis of angiogenesis-related gene interactions is a powerful tool for understanding the molecular basis of angiogenesis, and for facilitating drug development.
the gene functional association network is a valuable resource for understanding the complexity of angiogenic regulation and for developing more effective anti-angio-genetic therapeutics.
a global gene functional network can be used to predict the efficacy of a multi-targeted kinase inhibitor.
